finding.claim: Unauthenticated /logo endpoint fetches any URL that merely contains the substring 'example.io' and returns the full response body to the caller.
finding.source: main.go:31 raw := r.FormValue("logo") (attacker-controlled query or form value)
finding.sink: main.go:36 http.Get(raw), with response copied back at main.go:38 io.Copy(w, resp.Body)

trace.note: strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is a substring check, not a host allowlist
http.Get(raw) uses the default client: no scheme restriction, redirects followed, no host re-check
Response body streamed back to the attacker (non-blind)

finding.guards_checked: Substring check (main.go:32) does not close: it passes for 'example.io' in the path or query, and the host is never parsed. No scheme restriction. No loopback, RFC-1918, or link-local blocking. No authentication on the route. Redirects are not validated (main.go:36 uses the default client). The server binds all interfaces (main.go:44), so the route is publicly reachable.

verdict.guard_found: Only a substring check at main.go:32 (strings.Contains(raw, "example.io")), which does not parse the host and does not close the finding. No scheme restriction, no private/loopback/link-local blocking, no auth on the /logo route (main.go:43), and no CheckRedirect on the default client used at main.go:36. The noRedirect/trusted-host check at main.go:20-24 belongs to the /cdn handler, not /logo.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled logo value at main.go:31 reaches http.Get(raw) at main.go:36 after only a substring test at main.go:32, so a URL such as http://127.0.0.1:port/?example.io passes; the response is streamed back via io.Copy at main.go:38, and the server listens on all interfaces at main.go:44.
